sections.title: Clinical Pearl: Aniridia Management
content: Monitor for Aniridic Keratopathy (limbal stem cell deficiency).
Check for foveal hypoplasia via OCT to explain poor visual acuity.
Glaucoma occurs in 50-75% of cases; monitor IOP and discs regularly.

sections.title: Diode Laser Photocoagulation: Clinical Profile
content: • Raised IOP in poor vision patients
• Pain relief in blind eye with raised IOP
• Unsuccessful glaucoma filtration surgery or drainage implantation

sections.title: Trabeculectomy: Indications & Failure Risks
content: • Failure of conservative therapy to achieve IOP control
• Progressive deterioration despite adequate IOP control (including poor compliance)
• Primary therapy in a young patient with advanced disease
• Topical sympathomimetics use for over 3 years

rows: Alkylating agent; inhibits fibroblast proliferation and suppresses vascular ingrowth. Dose: 0.2mg/ml for 2 min (0.4mg/ml in high risk).
Retards DNA synthesis (inhibits fibroblasts). Intraop: 50mg/ml for 5 min. Postop: 0.1ml of 25mg/ml or 50mg/ml.

sections.title: Post-Trabeculectomy Complications
content: Causes of Shallow AC: Pupillary block, Overfiltration, Malignant Glaucoma
Endophthalmitis Risk Factors: Antimetabolite use, Inferiorly placed bleb, Bleb leak, Blepharitis, Conjunctivitis
Common Pathogens: Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Gram-negative organisms

sections.title: MIGS & Glaucoma Drainage Devices (GDD)
content: **MIGS Indications:** Mild-moderate glaucoma (slow loss, modest target 15-17 mmHg); Combined with Phaco/IOL to reduce topical meds.
**GDD Indications:** Severe conjunctival scarring; Uncontrolled glaucoma post-trab + MMC; Secondary glaucoma (Aniridia, NVG, ICE, traumatic AC disruption); Certain congenital glaucomas.

**GDD Complications:** Excessive drainage (hypotony + shallow AC); Bleb encapsulation (raised IOP 1-6 weeks post-op); Malposition (endothelial/lenticular touch -> corneal decompensation/cataract); Tube erosion; Early/Late drainage failure; Double vision (extraocular muscle interference).

sections.title: Final Review & Verbatim Notes
sections.content: All content provided has been mapped including specific doses like 0.2-0.5s for iridoplasty, specific pathogens like H. influenza, and surgical details like 12-24 burns for diode TSCPC. Success signs for PI include the 'gush of pigment debris', and for SLT, 'tiny champagne bubbles'. Mechanism for miotics includes pulling the peripheral iris away from the trabecular meshwork via sphincter contraction.
